- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in early forecast periods (first 5–10 days of 30d window).
- Forecasts tend to peak too early or too high after recent spikes, then sharply drop — suggesting overshoot and failure to capture mean reversion.
- Model underestimates prices in the latter half of the 30d window, particularly when true values are rising or stabilizing.
- Forecast bias is stronger when history includes recent sharp upward moves — model fails to adjust downward sufficiently.
- Model exhibits lag in responding to true price declines — often underestimates drops until they’re already underway.
- Forecasts show persistent overconfidence in upward momentum, especially when historical mean is declining.
- When true prices are trending upward, model often fails to anticipate the full magnitude of the rise — underestimates peak.
- Model tends to smooth out volatility, underestimating sharp drops and overestimating gradual declines.
- Forecasts are more accurate when the 30d history includes recent price consolidation or sideways movement — model performs worse during strong trending periods.
- Model overestimates prices when the 30d history includes recent high values — fails to recognize diminishing returns or mean reversion.
